## Purpose
`branch_state.rs`'s `PrLookup`/`PrEvidence`/`PrStatus`, and `pr_provider.rs`'s `PrProvider` trait plus its `PrView`/`PrOpened`/`PrChecks` structs, are the crate's canonical pull-request vocabulary. Every provider adapter (`pr_azure.rs`'s Azure REST client) normalises onto these shared types rather than exposing provider-specific words, so no caller ever re-reduces a provider's status vocabulary itself.

## Convention
Folder: apps/rt/src/shared/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 3
The three exemplars show a port/adapter split: `pr_provider.rs` declares the `PrProvider` trait and the shared `PrStatus`/`PrView` vocabulary as plain structs/enums with doc comments citing the exact upstream REST/CLI field names being normalised (`sourceRefName`, `headRefName`). `pr_azure.rs` is the ONLY place that spells the Azure REST API version, PAT env var, or `az`/`ureq` transport — it implements the port and maps every provider-specific word (`status_from_azure`) onto the shared `PrStatus`. An unimplemented provider operation answers a stable sentinel token (`PR_UNSUPPORTED`) rather than a fabricated absence.

## How to apply
A new PR-status or PR-action field is added to the shared port (`pr_provider.rs` or `branch_state.rs`), never to one adapter alone. A new provider adapter is a new file under `shared/` implementing `PrProvider`, containing every mention of that provider's API/CLI, with its own `status_from_<provider>` mapping function tested against the provider's documented enum values (see `status_from_azure`'s doc comment citing the REST contract).
